lead.headline: The US is about to propose new tariffs on 16 big trading partners, India among them, after a probe into excess factory capacity
lead.short: The Trump administration is poised to release the findings of a probe into alleged excess industrial capacity in 16 major US trading partners, including India and China, with new import duties on a wide range of goods expected, three people familiar with the matter told Reuters. The duties would stack on top of earlier tariffs.

why.text: India is still exposed to Washington's tariffs, and a new country-by-country levy could hit its exporters just as foreign money returns to its markets.

more: The duties would partly replace tariffs struck down by the US Supreme Court in February. The rates are unclear, but one person said they would be tailored to each country, with Mexico and Norway unlikely to face immediate levies. The US Trade Representative's office has been investigating under Section 301 of the Trade Act of 1974.

Ryan Majerus, a former senior Commerce Department official, said rates of 15% to 25% are possible, on top of existing tariffs of 10% or 12.5%. Caps agreed in trade deals, 15% for the EU, Japan and South Korea, are expected to be honoured. A Reuters/Ipsos poll after the midterms found 62% of Americans support repealing the tariffs.

seconds.headline: Trump says a pardon for Jensen Huang is "always an option" and urges him not to take the Fifth, as Nvidia gives back 6%
seconds.byline: TIMES OF INDIA · BBC · MINT · 25 NOV
seconds.short: Donald Trump said on Tuesday he was open to pardoning Nvidia's Jensen Huang but did not think it would be needed. "It's always an option, I guess, but I don't think it'll be necessary," he told the New York Post, urging Huang to "just tell the truth" when Congress questions him next week rather than invoke the Fifth Amendment.

why.text: Huang's fate is now tied to Trump's, and the president's open backing brings political risk for both.

more: Trump has taken a public victory lap. "I made the deal," he told CNBC, and posted an AI-generated image of Huang raising a fist in front of an Nvidia banner, surrounded by Secret Service guards, riffing on the photo taken after the 2024 attempt on his life. He called Huang "100% aboveboard" and "a very smart person".

Markets cooled. Nvidia fell more than 6% on Tuesday after soaring 31.5% on Monday, and the Nasdaq lost 1.4%. Anthropic fell more than 6% to just over $1 below its $83 IPO price, days after its record debut. "One headline doesn't really resolve investor questions about the AI trade," said Gene Goldman of Cetera Financial Group.

update.new: Trump floats a pardon; the rally fades.
update.front: Trump now says a pardon for Huang is an option.

seconds.headline: The Sensex rises 1.5% by 2pm after Tuesday's holiday as foreign money keeps coming, and the rupee hits a three-month high
seconds.short: The Sensex was up 1.5% at about 83,650 at 2pm on Wednesday, and the Nifty rose 1.6% to about 25,760, as Indian markets reopened after Tuesday's holiday. Earlier the Sensex jumped 2,062 points to a high of 84,498. Strong foreign buying, lower crude and gains in bank shares drove the rise, defying weak global markets.

why.text: Indian shares are within 1% of a three-month high, and the rupee is at its strongest in three months, as Wall Street wobbles.

more: Bajaj Finserv rose 5.7%, followed by Bajaj Finance, Trent, InterGlobe Aviation and Hindustan Unilever, while ICICI Bank and HDFC Bank gained over 3.5%. Titan and Tata Steel fell. Foreign investors bought ₹5,673 crore of shares on Monday, according to exchange data, and their November inflows are already a record.

The rupee strengthened to about 92.2 a dollar, from 92.91 at Monday's close. Traders had expected a firmer open on the revival in foreign appetite for Indian shares, and most bankers saw Monday's dip from a seven-month high as a healthy correction rather than a reversal. Brent crude traded 1.4% lower at about $90.

update.front: Shares have now bounced back after Monday's fall.

seconds.headline: Real Madrid come from behind to thrash PSV 5-1, with a wonder goal from Bellingham and two from Mbappé
seconds.short: Real Madrid beat PSV Eindhoven 5-1 at the Bernabéu on Tuesday night after going behind to a first-half penalty. Fede Valverde equalised, Jude Bellingham scored one of the goals of the season to put Madrid ahead after half-time, Kylian Mbappé added two and Vinícius Júnior scored on the break. Arda Güler made two assists.

why.text: It turned a dreadful first half into one of Madrid's biggest European wins of the season, and Bellingham's form is now the talk of the club.

more: José Mourinho replaced both centre-backs, Éder Militão and Antonio Rüdiger, at half-time, and also took off Aurélien Tchouaméni, who was on a yellow card. "I watched the first half: it was dreadful," Mourinho said. He showed the players three video clips at the break, one defensive and two attacking.

Bellingham credited his form to "Mourinho, full stop". Mourinho disagreed: "The person responsible for who Jude is, is Jude... and his team-mates." He called Bellingham "the best midfielder in the world" and said it was "a scandal" he was not in the Ballon d'Or top 10. Mbappé had nine shots, and Vinícius hit the post twice. Madrid host Alavés on Saturday.

update.front: Madrid have now won the match, 5-1.

stories.headline: The Supreme Court asks Delhi Police to respond to Umar Khalid's and Sharjeel Imam's bail pleas, and will weigh interim bail after hearing them
stories.short: The Supreme Court on Wednesday issued notice to Delhi Police on bail pleas by the activists Umar Khalid and Sharjeel Imam, who are charged under the anti-terror law UAPA over the 2020 Delhi riots. A bench headed by Chief Justice Surya Kant said it would consider their requests for interim bail only after hearing the police.

why.text: Both men have been in jail for years without trial, and the case has become a test of how long the anti-terror law allows people to be held.

more: The activists argue that the prosecution has failed to examine protected witnesses, and that a one-year embargo set earlier by the Supreme Court is about to expire. They are challenging a Delhi High Court order that denied them bail in the case over the alleged "larger conspiracy" behind the riots in north-east Delhi.

Imam's petition says the chargesheet was filed on 25 September 2020, with 18 accused and more than 900 witnesses, including 47 protected witnesses. He says that after six years and nine months as an undertrial, the prosecution has not examined a single witness. Khalid says his continued jailing would violate his right to life and liberty under Article 21.

stories.headline: The Congress tells the Samajwadi Party "we aren't begging" after the SP names candidates in the middle of seat talks
stories.short: The Congress's Uttar Pradesh working committee chief, Imran Masood, lashed out at the Samajwadi Party on Wednesday after it named candidates for five seats while seat-sharing talks for the 2027 assembly election are still going on. One of the SP's picks is in Saharanpur, Masood's own Lok Sabha constituency. "We aren't begging," Masood said.

why.text: The opposition alliance that hurt the BJP in Uttar Pradesh in 2024 is fraying before the state's biggest election.

more: "When you are holding talks on one hand and making announcements on the other, it shows that you are not serious," Masood said. He said he would discuss with the party leadership whether the talks with the SP should continue at all.

The SP offered the Congress 26 of the state's 403 seats on Tuesday, and its general secretary Ram Gopal Yadav said they included two the Congress won last time, four where it came second and 20 where the SP polled far more. The Congress rejected the offer, according to sources quoted by The Hindu. It had asked for about 100.

stories.headline: Kilmar Ábrego García, wrongly deported to El Salvador last year, leaves the US for Spain
stories.short: Kilmar Ábrego García, the Maryland man whose wrongful deportation to El Salvador in March 2025 became a flashpoint in the fight over Donald Trump's immigration policy, has left the US for Spain. After he was returned to face human trafficking charges, which were later dropped, the administration kept trying to send him to Uganda and Ghana.

why.text: His case became the clearest test of whether the administration would obey the courts on deportations.

more: "A year and a half ago, the Trump Administration wanted to leave Kilmar Ábrego García to rot in a Salvadoran gulag," said Senator Chris Van Hollen, who visited him in El Salvador's Cecot prison. "Today, Kilmar is travelling to a country of his choice, a free man." His lawyer said the move was "temporary" and that he would wait out the administration.

Ábrego García, who is married to a US citizen, came to the US illegally from El Salvador as a teenager. A judge granted him protection from deportation in 2019, citing the risk of persecution by a gang. After his removal, the Supreme Court ordered the government to facilitate his return, and the administration admitted he had been deported in error.

stories.headline: North Korea orders Switzerland's new office in Pyongyang shut and gives its head 48 hours to leave, over sanctions on a children's camp
stories.short: North Korea on Wednesday demanded the closure of Switzerland's diplomatic office in Pyongyang, opened only last month, and ordered its head, Astier Sylvain, to leave within 48 hours. It was protesting Swiss sanctions on the Songdowon International Children's Camp over its alleged role in taking in children from Russia-occupied parts of Ukraine.

why.text: It shuts one of the few Western windows into North Korea weeks after it opened, and shows how closely Pyongyang now guards its ties with Moscow.

more: A day earlier, Kim Yo Jong, the powerful sister of leader Kim Jong Un, threatened to close the office and condemned the sanctions. The Korean Central News Agency said a senior foreign ministry official summoned Sylvain, handed him the notice and declared him persona non grata. Reports have said some Ukrainian children abducted by Russian forces were sent to the camp to be reeducated.

Swiss foreign minister Ignazio Cassis travelled to North Korea in late October to open the office and held talks with his counterpart Choe Son Hui on "promoting dialogue and cooperation". North Korea has sent thousands of troops and large shipments of weapons to support Russia's invasion of Ukraine.

stories.headline: Shenzhou-24 lifts off with Muhammad Zeeshan Ali, making him Pakistan's first astronaut and China's first foreign crew member
stories.short: A Long March-2F rocket lifted off from China's Jiuquan launch centre at 05:48 IST on Wednesday carrying the Shenzhou-24 crew, including Muhammad Zeeshan Ali, a Pakistan Air Force pilot who becomes his country's first astronaut. In Islamabad, students and stargazers packed the space agency's auditorium before dawn and sang the national anthem as it rose.

why.text: It is the first time China has flown a foreigner in its crewed programme, and a sign of how close Beijing and Islamabad have grown.

more: Ali, 40, flies as a payload specialist with commander Tang Hongbo and flight engineer Wu Yi. The spacecraft was due to dock with the forward port of the Tiangong station's Tianhe core module after a rapid rendezvous of about three and a half hours. He will spend about a week on board, conducting experiments with the Chinese crew.

"I was so caught up in the moment that I forgot to record," said Zainab Abbasi, 21, a physics student watching at SUPARCO's headquarters, as the hall erupted in chants of "Pakistan Zindabad". Ali will return to Earth on Shenzhou-23, while one of that crew, Zhu Yangzhu, stays in orbit for a year.
